Abercrombie (ANF +19.69%) reported third quarter results reflecting its 16th consecutive quarter of sales growth, with management citing balanced performance across both brand families and all three geographic regions. The company stated that it is executing on strategic priorities including brand expansion, gross margin stabilization, and technological investment. Management reported that strong cash flow enabled continued share repurchases and reinvestment in the store fleet, with the company remaining on track for its fourth consecutive year of net sales growth.

Operator: Good day, and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the Abercrombie & Fitch Third Quarter Fiscal Year 2026 Earnings Call. [Operator Instructions] Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded. I would now like to hand the conference over to your first speaker, Mo Gupta, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Mohit (Mo) Gupta: Thank you. Good morning, and welcome to our Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Call. Joining me today on the call are Fran Horowitz, Chief Executive Officer; Scott Lipesky, Chief Operating Officer; and Robert J. Ball, Chief Financial Officer. Earlier this morning, we issued our third quarter earnings release, which is available on our website at corporate.abercrombie.com under the Investors section. Also available on our website is an investor presentation. Please keep in mind that we will make certain forward-looking statements on the call.

These statements are subject to the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995 and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from the expectations and assumptions we mentioned today. These factors and uncertainties are discussed in our reports and filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission. In addition, we'll be referring to certain non-GAAP financial measures during the call. Additional details and reconciliations of GAAP to adjusted non-GAAP financial measures are included in the release and the investor presentation issued earlier this morning. With that, I will turn the call over to Fran.

Fran Horowitz: Thanks, Mo, and thanks, everyone, for joining. I'm pleased to report another strong quarter for our business. Net sales grew 11% to a third quarter record of $1.4 billion, ahead of our expectations and our 16th consecutive quarter of growth. We've grown the business each quarter for 4 years running, and that momentum continues. You've heard me emphasize the importance of balance, and we demonstrated it again this quarter. All 3 regions and both brands delivered double-digit net sales growth with each seeing growth rate accelerate from second quarter levels. The strong top line, coupled with disciplined inventory management, enabled us to deliver healthy sales growth with higher AUR and lower promotions.

This performance flowed to the bottom line, where we delivered an operating margin of 15.5%, nicely above our expectations. And we continue to execute against our capital allocation priorities, investing in marketing, stores, digital and technology, all to support long-term growth while increasing net income per diluted share 62% year-over-year to $3.82. We also used our balance sheet to repurchase $100 million of shares in the quarter, bringing our year-to-date total to $382 million or 9% of shares outstanding at the beginning of the year. This marked our 11th straight quarter of share repurchases. Our teams continue to deliver for customers around the world, and we entered the important holiday season with momentum across brands and regions.

With that strong performance, we are raising our full year net sales and earnings expectations. We continue to expect fiscal 2026 to mark our fourth consecutive full year of net sales growth with consistent strong double-digit operating margins and significant cash return to shareholders through share repurchases. Turning back to the quarter. All 3 regions delivered double-digit net sales growth. The Americas grew 11% with stable traffic trends as we moved from back-to-school into fall. EMEA delivered 12% net sales growth with comparable sales up 4%, a significant sequential improvement from the second quarter. Germany performance improved nicely as the team continued to dial in marketing, promotions and inventory to customer traffic and demand.

Sources indicate that several other European markets returned to growth on healthy conversion trends, and the U.K. continues to be a consistent growth market. APAC performed ahead of our expectations again this quarter, growing 24% on strong traffic, particularly in stores. While still evaluating the right go-to-market strategies in the APAC region, the team has continued to invest in marketing and manage inventory, and we've seen stronger top line performance, especially in Hollister. Diving further into the brands, Hollister had a great back-to-school season to start the quarter and carried that momentum throughout, delivering 11% net sales growth on top of 16% growth and record third quarter sales last year.

It has been revealed that as we discussed last quarter, the team prioritized receipts heading into back-to-school to support customer demand, and we continue to Read & React as the season progressed. That discipline allowed us to keep inventory tight, reduce promotional levels and deliver higher AUR. Growth was balanced across men's and women's with fleece, knits, graphics and bottoms performing well. Hollister's denim campaign with rising star Freya Skye drove strong social engagement and positive fan response to events in both the U.S. and U.K., demonstrating the power of connecting with our customers with culturally relevant talent and experiences.

Recent findings suggest that following a strong third quarter, Hollister is bringing an exciting flow of newness throughout the holiday season, including latest product drops at Target as our continued partnership gives us another way to reach new and existing customers. In our owned and operated stores, we've invested to ensure our customers have the latest brand experience. Year-to-date, we've opened 23 new stores and remodeled or rightsized 48 Hollister stores, a substantial portion of our fleet. Overall, Hollister has made considerable progress, and we're excited for what the brand can do to cap off 2026. At Abercrombie brands, we had an excellent transition into fall with net sales growing 12% and accelerating nicely from the second quarter.

Inventory remained tightly managed and strong product acceptance allowed us to deliver improved AUR and lower-than-expected promotions. Growth was balanced across men's and women's and across tops and bottoms. Women's knits and sweaters performed particularly well, while men's saw strength across jeans and pants. Our active assortment under Your Personal Best continues to perform well. We recently showcased YPB through a partnership with Barry's, the fast-growing global fitness brand, bringing a collection of studio-ready activewear to its highly engaged community through Barry's studios and our direct channels. Abercrombie's momentum extends to our store fleet, an integral part of how customers experience the brand.

According to recent reports, our A&F SoHo store has continued to exceed expectations since opening in July with YPB, footwear and accessories all part of the experience. We've already brought elements of that modern A&F expression to 15 stores in major markets just in time for holiday. We're midway through another successful season with the NFL, connecting with fans in more ways across product, partnerships and experiences. As an official fashion partner of the NFL, the Dallas Cowboys and Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, we're engaging fans at game time events and offering our NFL assortment at select stadiums and on nflshop.com. And in time for holiday, we recently rolled out a collection co-designed with Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb.

The NFL assortment also extends to abercrombie kids with styles for boys and girls. As we move into the holiday season, we're offering a fresh digital gift card on the Abercrombie app and website, featuring ideas for every age from babies and toddlers to major kids and adults. Creating memorable holiday experiences has been part of Abercrombie for more than 130 years, and we're building on that heritage in new and relevant ways as we look to finish the year strong. In addition to our strong quarterly results, we've made meaningful progress against our 4 priorities for the year.

It has been revealed that that includes growing our brands and owned and operated business while adding fresh avenues of growth, stabilizing gross margins against external cost pressures, investing in tools and technologies like AI to improve speed and efficiency and maintaining strong profitability to fuel excess cash return to shareholders through share repurchases. On that first priority, our growth continues to start with the customer, a consistent focus that has resulted in net sales growth every quarter for 4 consecutive years. Our teams have stayed close throughout the year, testing, learning and evolving our assortments alongside engaging marketing across brands and regions.

Industry observers note that we've invested meaningfully in stores and digital to improve the customer experience while partnerships and newly introduced product categories are helping us reach new customers. While early, it's really encouraging to see how our evolved model is driving brand love, awareness and consideration even in well-established markets like the U.S. It's also exciting to see how we can make this much progress on global brand growth, including new partnerships and categories for our brands while still balancing our other 3 business priorities. We've been able to manage inventory and control promotions by focusing on giving the customer the fashion and fit they value, which has enabled gross margin improvement despite freight cost pressure.

We've continued to invest in our digital systems and infrastructure, including deploying AI-based solutions across the customer journey, which we believe is critical to brand health and relevance. And of course, with our strong culture of financial discipline, we've been able to keep our double-digit operating margins and also repurchased 9% of shares outstanding year-to-date. Three quarters in, 2026 has been a year of consistent profitable growth. That momentum, along with a strong start to November, has led us to increase our full year sales and profitability outlook.

We now expect to deliver our fourth consecutive year of net sales growth, another year of strong double-digit operating margins and growth in net income per diluted share while maintaining our target of returning at least $500 million to shareholders through share repurchases. The consistency of our results reflects the strength of our operating model, the health of our global brands and the financial discipline of this team. To our associates around the world, thank you for everything you do to deliver for our customers every day. I'm incredibly proud of what we continue to accomplish together. We're ready for holiday and a strong finish to 2026, and we look forward to updating you all on both in early March.

And with that, I'll hand it over to Robert.

Robert J. Ball: Thanks, Fran, and good morning, everyone. I'd also like to thank our teams around the world for another strong quarter and the work they've done to position us for the holiday season. We delivered record third quarter net sales of $1.44 billion, up 11% year-over-year and above the 5% to 6% growth range we provided in August. Comparable sales increased 6% and AUR grew high single digits, supported by lower promotional activity, driving better-than-expected results to our outlook. We're particularly encouraged by the quality and balance of that growth. Both brands in all 3 regions delivered double-digit net sales growth with sequential acceleration across the business. Starting with our regions.

Recent findings suggest that net sales increased 11% in the Americas, 12% in EMEA and 24% in APAC. Comparable sales increased 5% in the Americas, 4% in EMEA and 24% in APAC. By brand, Abercrombie brands net sales increased 12% with comparable sales up 6%. Hollister delivered 11% net sales growth against last year's record with comparable sales up 5%. Both brands grew net sales across all 3 regions. Across regions and brands, the spread between net sales growth and comparable sales was driven by net new stores and third-party channel performance. Importantly, we're seeing contributions from multiple sources of growth. Our existing direct-to-consumer business continues to perform, while the new stores and third-party distribution partnerships are providing incremental opportunities to reach customers.

Industry observers note that that combination is encouraging as we think about the durability of our growth. Turning to profitability. Third quarter operating income was $223 million, and operating margin was 15.5% of sales, above the 13% to 14% outlook we provided in August. Our results included approximately $20 million of IEEPA tariff refunds, contributing around 150 basis points to operating margin, consistent with our outlook. But importantly, the underlying business also performed ahead of our expectations. At the midpoint of our outlook, operating margin exceeded expectations by approximately 200 basis points, driven primarily by stronger gross margin performance from higher AUR with additional benefit from expense leverage. Year-over-year, operating margin increased approximately 350 basis points from 12% in the third quarter of 2025.

It has been revealed that of that improvement, approximately 150 basis points came from tariff refunds and approximately 80 basis points came from lower year-over-year tariff expense on products sold in the quarter. Higher Q3 AUR was mostly offset by higher freight, so the remaining approximately 100 basis points of operating margin improvement came from operating expense leverage, particularly from marketing and fulfillment and selling expense. We're encouraged by our operating margin performance. Higher AUR and disciplined promotional activity are supporting gross margins, while continued expense management is allowing us to invest in the business and maintain strong profitability. And importantly, we're delivering that performance while continuing to make investments in stores, digital capabilities and the infrastructure needed to support future growth.

Moving below operating income. Our tax rate for the quarter was 29%, better than expected, primarily due to stronger international performance. Net income per diluted share was $3.82 compared with diluted earnings per share of $2.36 last year and above our outlook of $2.90 to $3.20. Both our third quarter outlook and results include approximately $0.40 per share of benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds. We do not currently anticipate any additional IEEPA tariff refunds, and we updated the table in the press release and investor presentation with additional detail on the timing of tariff refunds and ongoing tariff expense. Turning to inventory and the balance sheet.

Ending inventory at cost increased around 4% year-over-year with units up mid-single digits and aligned with our expectations for unit sales growth. We believe inventory remains appropriately positioned as we enter the holiday season, giving our teams flexibility to respond to consumer demand while maintaining promotional discipline. On the balance sheet, we ended the quarter with $724 million of cash and cash equivalents and approximately $1.2 billion of liquidity. During the quarter, we repurchased $100 million worth of shares, bringing year-to-date repurchases to $382 million and our 11th consecutive quarter of share repurchases. Year-to-date, that represents approximately 9% of beginning of year shares outstanding. We ended the quarter with $468 million remaining on our current repurchase authorization.

In a recent development, our approach to capital allocation remains consistent. We're investing in the business to support profitable growth, maintaining a strong balance sheet and returning excess cash to shareholders. Turning to the outlook. Our strong third quarter performance and expectations for higher fourth quarter demand support an increase to our full year sales and EPS outlook. As a reminder, our full year outlook includes the entire $120 million of tariff refunds recognized during the second and third quarters. We estimate that the refund will contribute approximately 220 basis points to full year operating margin and approximately $2.15 to full year diluted earnings per share.

Separate from the refunds, our outlook continues to reflect current Section 301 tariff rates of 10% to 12.5% effective on global imports into the U.S. Based on those assumptions, we continue to expect approximately 10 basis points of year-over-year gross margin favorability from lower year-over-year tariff expense on sold product, which we expect to be more than offset by higher freight costs. For the full year, we now expect net sales growth of around 6% from the $5.27 billion in 2025, with growth across regions and brands. We now expect mid-single-digit AUR improvement for the full year and approximately 20 basis points of benefit to net sales from foreign currency.

We continue to expect full year operating margin in the range of 14.5% to 15%, including approximately 220 basis points of benefit from the IEEPA tariff refunds. We're forecasting a tax rate around 28%, diluted weighted average shares of around 44 million and net income per diluted share in the range of $13.70 to $13.90. The EPS outlook includes an estimated $2.15 from IEEPA tariff refunds. For capital allocation, we expect capital expenditures around $260 million. We remain on track to deliver approximately 130 new store experiences, including 50 new stores and 80 remodels and rightsizes against approximately 20 closures.

These investments remain an important part of our growth strategy, allowing us to expand our reach while improving productivity and customer experience of our existing fleet. We continue to expect at least $500 million of share repurchases for 2026. For the fourth quarter of 2026, we expect net sales growth of around 7% from the Q4 2025 level of $1.67 billion with growth across regions and brands. We expect a fourth quarter operating margin around 15%, a modest expansion from the fourth quarter of 2025. This is largely in line with our prior outlook, but has been updated to reflect some incremental freight expense of around 100 basis points.

Sources indicate that despite the increase in freight, we continue to expect modest gross margin improvement year-over-year, partially offset by modest expense deleverage, mainly from incentive compensation. We expect a fourth quarter tax rate of around 28% and net income per diluted share in the range of $4.40 to $4.60. Diluted weighted average shares are expected to be around 43 million, including the anticipated impact of at least $120 million of fourth quarter share repurchases. To close, we are pleased with our third quarter results and the consistency of execution we've delivered throughout 2026. We've now delivered 16 consecutive quarters of sales growth, and we're doing it while maintaining strong profitability, investing in the business and returning significant capital to shareholders.

Sources indicate that what gives us conviction in our model isn't just our performance in any single quarter, but it's also our consistency. We're seeing healthy, sustained growth across our core business, expanding our reach through newly introduced stores and partnerships and maintaining the financial discipline needed to support both. As we look ahead, we're focused on adding to this track record while investing in the opportunities that can drive our next chapter of growth. We believe that we're well positioned to finish 2026 strong and carry that momentum into 2027, and we look forward to covering both in early March. With that, operator, we're ready for questions.

Claude can ship code for you now – how to try it (if you dare)

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (886 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, developers are already using Claude Code and other AI-powered coding tools like OpenAI’s Codex in droves, but some still want to check code themselves before pushing it.
  • Industry observers note that with Claude Ship, announced in beta Monday, “Claude can now review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows,” Anthropic remarked.
  • Also: How I made a paid Mac app in 11 days with Claude – without writing a single line of code.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, developers are already using Claude Code and other AI-powered coding tools like OpenAI’s Codex in droves, but some still want to check code themselves before pushing it. A upcoming feature from Anthropic is banking on more adventurous, agent-first coders being comfortable with handing even that last step off to AI.

Industry observers note that with Claude Ship, announced in beta Monday, “Claude can now review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows,” Anthropic remarked. The feature is geared toward individual developers or companies who want to move faster or already delegate a significant amount of coding tasks to agents.

Also: How I made a paid Mac app in 11 days with Claude – without writing a single line of code.

According to recent reports, “Teams stay in control of where it runs and which changes need a person,” Anthropic noted. “The goal: ship code as fast as teams write it.”.

The new feature uses two new agents alongside Code Review, which Anthropic released in March for Teams and Enterprise plans. Code Review first collects, organizes, and posts findings to a PR. Then, Anthropic said, the agents, PR Steward and Claude Approvals, guide a PR “through review, fixes, and an approval decision so teams don’t have to manage each step manually.”.

PR Steward can’t approve or merge pull requests, designed instead to participate “on failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback from Code Review, other review tools, or team members.” It also documents what it changed in each push through comments and provides instructions for how to undo it, should developers want to. Throughout the process, developers can give Claude instructions or tell it to stop by commenting @claude.

Also: I tried replacing Claude Code with a local AI stack that’s completely free – how it went.

As a final step, Claude Approvals references whatever policy the user or team abides by (which developers provide as a repo file), and additional signals developers set, like Code Review findings, before approving changes autonomously if allowed. If not, it will seek out “deeper human sign-off,” Anthropic stated.

“It works like a smarter CODEOWNERS file,” the release added. Anthropic said it recommends that most customers enable those additional checks “first in observe-only mode to build confidence before configuring branch protection to require Claude Approvals’ green light.”.

Admins can select which repos the feature runs in and adjust settings as needed.

But Claude Ship isn’t meant for everyone.

“Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” Anthropic noted in the release, noting that its own Claude Code team uses Claude to write a majority of the code it needs.

ZDNET senior contributing editor David Gewirtz mentioned the idea of shipping code at the speed of writing it “raises the hair on the back of my neck.” But he added that, given how impressive Claude Code has been thus far, he wouldn’t be surprised if Anthropic’s deployment tools were equally effective.

Also: Claude Code vs. Codex: Why I use both and how to choose one (if you must).

“But, it does depend on the team’s workflow and the kind of development they’re doing,” he mentioned. “It’s not something for every team and certainly not for every indy developer, but for certain deployment processes, it could shave a ton of time off turnaround, saving money and potentially sending fixes to customers much faster. ‘Tis cool.”.

Ultimately, Gewirtz remarked he has reasons to both trust the tool and be concerned about what it means for younger developers in the workplace.

“Since that workflow is often assigned to less experienced members of the team, it’s likely that Claude would be as accurate, although it’s one more way to shut the junior members out of where they add value to the manufacturer and grow their skills to become senior decision makers,” he stated.

Developer platforms overall are adapting to the new state of the industry. Entire, a GitHub competitor started by the Microsoft-owned platform’s former CEO, is built around the expectation that developers are working side-by-side with agents.

Individuals with a Pro, Max, or Ultra subscription can use the /ship command now available in Claude Code, meaning “owners won’t notice any significant increase in token usage,” an Anthropic representative explained. Team and Enterprise users can use Claude Ship for Github repos, and it is billed on tokens, so your overall bill may change.

Industry observers note that still, that depends on the number of PRs users are putting through Claude Ship — to avoid any surprises, admins can set spending limits for both Code Review and the newly introduced PR Steward agent. They can also turn Claude Ship on for an entire repo, meaning developers won’t need the /ship command.

Anthropic added that certain Enterprise organizations “can claim at least $10,000 in Claude Ship credits to use within 30 days of claiming” by Jan. 15, 2027.

Also: How I safely run my OpenClaw AI agent 24/7 on a Mac – with Claude Code standing guard.

As with other Claude features, like the still-to-come Meetings, customers with a zero-data-retention policy and other privacy configurations don’t have access to Claude Ship.

CNET Survey: $75 Billion in Packages Could Be at Risk of Holiday Porch Theft

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1596 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Significant holiday sales, like Black Friday and Cyber Monday, are here, but before you click ‘buy,’ make sure you have a blueprint to protect your package from porch pirates.
  • CNET’s annual package theft survey polls US adults about their experiences with porch pirates and how they try to prevent thefts.
  • According to recent reports, but leaving your packages up for grabs could be a massive risk — especially when thieves know holiday gifts are being delivered.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Significant holiday sales, like Black Friday and Cyber Monday, are here, but before you click ‘buy,’ make sure you have a blueprint to protect your package from porch pirates.

CNET’s annual package theft survey polls US adults about their experiences with porch pirates and how they try to prevent thefts. This year, the average package value is $276.24, and 28% of US adults have had a package stolen, know someone who has or caught an attempted theft within the past year. Yet 20% of US adults don’t use security devices due to hardware costs or monthly subscription fees.

According to recent reports, but leaving your packages up for grabs could be a massive risk — especially when thieves know holiday gifts are being delivered. On the other hand, some bad actors don’t seem to mind being caught in the act on home security cameras, so are they really enough to deter bad actors? And what more can you do to protect your deliveries?

In a recent development, CNET’s findings show that some US adults have dealt with porch theft firsthand: 8% had packages meant for themselves or their households stolen within the past year, and 5% had a delivered gift stolen. Very few (1%) caught a theft in the act on a video doorbell or security camera.

Meanwhile, many US adults know someone who fell victim to package theft — 13% know a neighbor or community member who had a package stolen within the past year, and 12% know someone who doesn’t live in their community who has.

“Close to a third of our respondents are personally acquainted with package theft, which is still a high number compared to other complications like break-ins,” mentioned CNET’s senior home security editor, Tyler Lacoma. “Thieves generally look for crimes of opportunity, and few things are easier than a package left on a doorstep, especially if nobody is home.”.

Surprisingly, most US adults (72%) haven’t experienced package theft or know anyone who has.

Even though the percentages above may seem low, Lacoma said that package theft typically increases during the holidays when thieves know more deliveries are likely, and fresh porch theft tactics are always on the horizon.

There are reports of thieves trying Wi-Fi jamming to disable live security camera footage while they steal packages. And findings show that some are installing spy cams in high-value neighborhoods to learn your home’s layout and habits to take your packages shortly after they’re delivered. In recent years, pirates have even tracked shipping labels for high-value tech, like iPhones, to steal the package within minutes of arrival.

Industry observers note that so while the majority of US adults haven’t fallen victim, that shouldn’t be a sign to shrug off the concern or relax your home security measures. Instead, now’s the time to strategy how to safely store your packages if they’re delivered while you’re away.

According to recent reports, online shopping and deliveries to your door can be a convenient way to check off holiday wish lists, but the average package value this holiday season is less than last year. CNET found that US adults strategy to have an average of $276.24 in holiday packages delivered during this holiday season. That’s $23.82 less than last year’s average of $300.06.

It has been revealed that by generation, Millennials also have a lower estimated average package value than last year, with an average of $227.25, compared to their 2025 package value of $307.47 — an $80.22 difference, while Gen Z’s package value is only about $7 less than last year. But any package’s value is still worth taking precautions to help prevent it from being stolen.

It has been revealed that lacoma has thoughts on why that might be. In short, lower spending could mean fewer packages.

It has been revealed that “I wonder if people have also simply gotten fewer packages in general this year due to tariffs, inflation and tech prices. That could pull these numbers down,” said Lacoma. But there’s a high chance that could be the case considering CNET’s 2026 annual holiday survey, which found that US adult tech spending is down to $808 — which is $123 less than last year’s average of $931.

Thieves may not always know what’s in boxes they’re stealing but they’re willing to take a chance. We asked US adults which items were stolen in package thefts in the past year to give you a sense of what’s at risk.

Among the items stolen, apparel and accessories were the most common goods stolen (40%). That’s followed by toys and games (23%). Then there are everyday home basics, like decor, cookware and small appliances (19%).

According to recent reports, but personal tech devices and accessories are still among the items stolen. Small accessories like phone chargers and cases are most common (16%) among tech-related packages stolen. They are followed by audio gadgets like headphones and Bluetooth speakers, along with streaming devices and soundbars (11%, respectively).

Still, more costly tech like gaming consoles (10%), computers and laptops (9%) and smart home devices (6%) are among devices stolen.

You shouldn’t leave your packages up to chance. That’s why Lacoma recommends a few safer options to ensure your packages are stored securely after they’re delivered, even beyond keeping an eye on your doorbell or security camera. Instead, keep your packages out of sight with tactics like a delivery box with a code or key or ask for an in-garage delivery.

It has been revealed that “Delivery boxes have reached a fresh level of popularity in recent years as an effective way to stop porch pirates completely. However, Amazon’s Key service that delivers to your garage is an alternative,” said Lacoma. “Either way, you’ll need to trust delivery people to handle your shipments, unless you want to arrange for pickup at a nearby shipping center, which some people like to combine with other holiday errands.”.

If you don’t want to install a new security feature, try scheduling your packages to arrive when you know you’re home, requiring a signature from someone you trust or changing your delivery location to a pickup spot, like UPS’ Hold for Pick-Up locations or Amazon Lockers.

Home surveillance, like outdoor security cameras and video doorbells, can deter package thieves who don’t want to risk getting caught on camera. But US adults have mixed feelings about their effectiveness in protecting against package theft.

According to recent reports, there are two deterrents that are keeping US adults from having security devices — cost and privacy. Findings show that 20% of US adults lack home security measures due to hardware costs or monthly subscription fees. That’s followed by 9% who don’t want to use cameras because of privacy concerns.

In a recent development, “Fortunately, the right home security picks can solve both these problems,” said Lacoma. “Brands like Tapo, Eufy, Aqara and even Google Nest offer package detection and alerts for free, so you don’t have to worry about extra fees.”.

Industry observers note that if you’re looking for a camera that’s off-the-grid, consider the Arlo Go 2. It’s an LTE camera, so it uses a cellular data connection instead of Wi-Fi. It still finds a signal, supports app operation and live video viewing. If you’re looking for a power-over-Ethernet camera that uses a cable connection, the Reolink Duo 3 is a good choice.

It has been revealed that lacoma added that many companies also offer ways to use local video storage and local AI detection so nothing is stored in the cloud. There are also features, such as customizable privacy zones, to minimize privacy concerns when used with the right precautions.

Industry observers note that among all US adults, only 14% have security devices with a monthly subscription that lets them save or playback video. By comparison, 12% have security devices but no subscription.

Sources indicate that those percentages could be low for a few reasons, including the overall perception of how helpful surveillance and security really are against porch theft. Eleven percent of US adults don’t think security devices deter porch thefts. It’s a valid concern since 4% fell victim to package theft or an attempted theft despite having security devices. And some US adults (9%) use security devices to get proof of a theft after the fact — not to prevent it.

But that doesn’t mean you should ignore the possibility of package theft — especially during the holidays. Even if you don’t want to install cameras or latest security devices, make a plan to protect your packages and avoid the headache of package theft over the holidays.

Sources indicate that “Remember, the simple presence of a security camera is enough to make many thieves look elsewhere – interviews have confirmed it,” remarked Lacoma. “And with today’s phone alerts about package detection, you can usually check on a package only seconds after it appears, or bring up footage if it unexpectedly vanishes, letting you take action fast. Fresh practices like delivery boxes or in-garage delivery help address risks in concrete ways, too.”.

CNET commissioned YouGov Plc to conduct the survey. All figures, unless otherwise stated, are from YouGov Plc. The total sample size was 2,016 adults. Fieldwork was undertaken between Oct. 23–27, 2026. The survey was carried out online. The figures have been weighted and are representative of all US adults (aged 18 plus).

The $75 billion figure was calculated by multiplying the average value of deliveries each US adult expects to receive by the 2025 US population of adults ages 18 and over calculated by the US Census Bureau.

Sources indicate that hecla Mining (HL -2.68%), a silver and gold miner, closed at $10.90, down 2.7%. Silver miners were under pressure in premarket trading after silver prices fell on rate-hike concerns, and investors are watching metal prices and upcoming management commentary.Trading volume reached 48.6M shares, coming in about 5% above its three-month average of 32.3M shares.

It has been revealed that S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) fell 0.5% to 7,201.09, while the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX: ^IXIC) dropped 1.5% to 23,73.54. Among silver and gold mining peers, Pan American Silver (PAAS -3.87%) closed at $31.07, down 3.9%, and Coeur Mining (CDE -2.27%) finished at $11.19, down 2.3%.

Sources indicate that hecla Mining's stock, like other precious metal mining companies, is sensitive to commodity prices and interest rates. Naturally, higher commodity prices typically translate into increased revenue. However, interest rates also feed into commodity prices.

Typically, they move in opposite directions. That's because they become less attractive as interest rates move higher since physical commodities don't earn anything. Holding other assets, such as bonds or dividend-paying stocks, becomes more attractive in higher-interest rate environments.

In a recent development, earlier this month, Hecla Mining reported third-quarter results. Sales grew more than 18% from the second quarter to $394.8 million. Management provided guidance on production and costs, but investors will likely focus on macroeconomic problems that affect commodity prices until the next quarterly earnings release.

    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Dell Just Reported Earnings and Raised Its Forecast by $10 Billion. Is the Stock a Buy After Tuesday's Selloff?

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (790 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Dell Technologies (DELL -11.83%) shares rose about 3% to $305 in after-hours trading Tuesday after the company reported that quarterly revenue more than doubled and raised its full-year forecast.
    • Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE -16.31%) led that decline.
    • Recent findings suggest that dell's earnings release for the quarter ended Oct.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jonathan Ponciano – Nov 24, 2026 at 4:54PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Dell Technologies ›.

    Dell Technologies (DELL -11.83%) shares rose about 3% to $305 in after-hours trading Tuesday after the company reported that quarterly revenue more than doubled and raised its full-year forecast. The stock had closed at $295.28 in the regular session, down 12% from Monday's $334.91, as AI hardware shares sold off.

    Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE -16.31%) led that decline. Its shares fell about 16% after executives stated on Monday's earnings call that memory and other components could stay scarce through at least the second half of 2028. HPE also guided for its cloud and AI business to keep about 14% of sales as operating profit in fiscal 2027, down from 18.4% in the quarter it just reported. Dell, which sells many of the same servers, fell with it.

    Recent findings suggest that dell's earnings release for the quarter ended Oct. 30 showed revenue of $54.9 billion, up 103% from a year earlier. And adjusted earnings rose 265% to $9.45 per share, well above the $6.59 analysts expected.

    Most of the growth came from the Infrastructure Solutions Group, which sells servers, networking, and storage. Its revenue tripled to $42.0 billion. AI-optimized server sales rose 291% to $22.0 billion, and traditional servers and networking rose 235% to $15.0 billion. "We are now a different manufacturer," Vice Chairman and Chief Operating Officer Jeff Clarke said in the release.

    Dell booked $60.2 billion of AI orders in the quarter and ended it with a record AI backlog of $132.3 billion, about two-thirds of the revenue it expects for the whole year.

    Gross margin was 21% of revenue, up from 20.7% a year earlier. Helping to drive that increase, the infrastructure business kept 17% of its sales as operating profit, compared with 12.4% a year ago, and its operating income quadrupled to $7.1 billion.

    Industry observers note that lower spending also helped. Operating expenses fell to 7.5% of revenue from 12.9%, and Chief Financial Officer David Kennedy remarked that is driving "higher profitability, even as AI servers become a larger part of our business." AI servers tend to carry thinner margins than storage, so a rising AI share usually pulls margins down, but this quarter it clearly didn't.

    On the other hand, PCs were the weak spot. The Client Solutions Group grew revenue by 3% to $12.9 billion, consumer sales fell by 15%, and the segment's operating income slipped by 6% to $704 million.

    Dell raised its full-year revenue forecast by $10 billion to $202 billion, up 78% from last year, and its AI server sales forecast to $78 billion from $74 billion. It now expects adjusted earnings of $29.68 per share, up from $25.50. For the fourth quarter, it guided revenue to $56.3 billion and adjusted earnings to $8.40 per share.

    Separately, the company returned a record $4.9 billion to shareholders through buybacks and dividends in the quarter, and its board approved an additional $25 billion in repurchases. Free cash flow rose to $3.5 billion from $506 million a year earlier.

    Inventories rose to $29.4 billion on Oct. 30 from $10.4 billion at the end of January, and total debt rose to $37.7 billion from $31.5 billion. If component costs keep climbing, as HPE expects, Dell may need to keep raising prices, and one quarter of higher margins doesn't show it can do that indefinitely.

    According to recent reports, the stock is also volatile. It rose about 20% on Monday after Nvidia (NVDA -5.86%) reinstated CEO Jensen Huang, then gave back most of that gain on Tuesday.

    Even after Tuesday's after-hours gain, the stock trades at about 10 times the adjusted earnings Dell expects for the fiscal year ending in January. That's a low multiple for a organization whose revenue just doubled and whose backlog covers much of next year. And while the stock fell on worries about a rival's margins, Dell's own margins rose.

    Industry observers note that the case depends on AI spending holding up, the same bet behind most AI stocks. Investors who already own plenty of semiconductor stocks and other AI infrastructure names should know Dell adds to that exposure rather than diversifying it. Those who want to see whether component costs hit margins can wait for next quarter's report.

The tech giant reported that its government services and defense investments remain a high-conviction sector due to durable federal funding and resilient cash flow profiles.

Private equity sponsors remain active, and we are seeing a growing pipeline of attractive opportunities across both upcoming originations as well as add-on investments. We are optimistic that activity levels will remain strong throughout the end of the year and into next year. We expect increased transaction activity to drive repayments across the portfolio, including opportunities to monetize equity co-investments and to redeploy that capital into income-generating investments. In the core middle market, the pricing for high-quality first lien term loans remains attractive, typically ranging from SOFR plus 500 to 550 basis points, with leverage of approximately 4.5x EBITDA.

    According to recent reports, importantly, these structures continue to include meaningful covenant protections, which is in contrast to the covenant-light structures prevalent in the upper middle market. We believe the current environment favors lenders with established private equity sponsor relationships, consistent access to deal flow, and disciplined underwriting. These are longstanding strengths of the PennantPark platform. We continue to believe that the core middle market offers an attractive risk-adjusted opportunity. Companies in this segment generally have EBITDA of $10 million-$50 million and often operate below the practical threshold of the broadly syndicated loan and high-yield markets.

    As a result, lenders can typically conduct extensive diligence, negotiate meaningful financial covenants, structure transactions with appropriate leverage and equity cushions, and maintain regular access to company financial information. Since our inception nearly 19 years ago, PNNT has invested $9.9 billion at an average yield of 11.1%, while maintaining a loss ratio on invested capital of roughly 20 basis points annually, a testament to our consistent and disciplined approach through multiple market cycles. As a provider of strategic capital who fuels the growth of our portfolio companies, in many cases, we participate in the upside of that company by making an equity co-investment.     • It has been revealed that on Tuesday, Bambu Lab took the wraps off its third-generation 3D printer, the P3C.
    • Industry observers note that the big deal here is the introduction of the Swaptek 7-tool changer, which allows you to switch to a different color or material in just 6 seconds, preventing you from having to stop and clean the nozzle every time.
    • In a recent development, the tool changer technology also allows you to mix different materials with less of a fuss, so you can use a typical rigid plastic and something like a flexible rubber in a single pass without stopping.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that on Tuesday, Bambu Lab took the wraps off its third-generation 3D printer, the P3C. It brings to the mainstream the company’s “tool changer” technology, which was previously reserved for higher-end, flagship models like the $2,500 H3C. Given the P3C costs less than half the bigger model, it might be the perfect gift to get your favorite 3D printing hobbyist for Black Friday.

    Industry observers note that the big deal here is the introduction of the Swaptek 7-tool changer, which allows you to switch to a different color or material in just 6 seconds, preventing you from having to stop and clean the nozzle every time. The technology produces significantly less waste and allows you to create faster prints.

    In a recent development, the tool changer technology also allows you to mix different materials with less of a fuss, so you can use a typical rigid plastic and something like a flexible rubber in a single pass without stopping. It can switch between different nozzle sizes in one job. You can switch between  0.2 mm, 0.4 mm, 0.6 mm and 0.8 mm midprint.

    The P3C ships with an integrated sealed AMS 3P filament management system that can store up to seven spools, each of which is on an independent feed path to the printer. You can also connect up to four external AMS units, supporting up to 22 colors.

    The P3C is more than just a 3D printer. The Swaptek system supports interchangeable craft tools, letting you cut, draw or emboss on materials.

    Bambu Lab also included a few features that make the P3C more approachable to newcomers. The P3C provides full-auto calibration, automatically aligning nozzle offsets and multi-tool heads so you don’t have to do it yourself. There’s also a built-in AI monitoring system that can detect challenges like nozzle clogs and purge-bin jams early on. A new health management system will no longer spit out vague or obscure errors when something goes wrong. Instead, the new system will explain the matter in plain language and provide step-by-step troubleshooting right on the screen.

    Recent findings suggest that CNET’s 3D printing expert, James Bricknell, hasn’t been able to test Bambu Labs’ latest model yet but is excited about it. “While the P3C didn’t arrive in time for a hands-on, it’s built with the same design language and hardware support as the recently released H3C. If it is anywhere near as good, and I think that’s likely, it’ll be at the top of any serious 3D printing enthusiast’s wish list.”.

    In a recent development, the P3C 3D printer AMS combo is available now worldwide for $1,149. The combo includes the printer, AMS 3P as well as 5 0.4mm standard PrintTools. Two slots are left open for you to customize. This combo option comes with virtually everything you need to get started printing your works of art and more.

    #188296. A Human and an AI Model (Apparently) Solved the Riemann Hypothesis: What it Means for Future of Math

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2178 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

    A Human and an AI Model (Apparently) Solved the Riemann Hypothesis: What it Means for Future of Math

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2178 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, the Riemann Hypothesis is one of math’s oldest and most famous unsolved problems.
    • Alpöge made the announcement on Friday in a four-page document (PDF) on his personal web page.
    • In a recent development, “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Alpöge said in the announcement.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, the Riemann Hypothesis is one of math’s oldest and most famous unsolved problems. It was originally put forward as a problem in 1859 by Bernhard Riemann, and professional and amateur mathematicians alike have made thousands of attempts to solve it. Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge has apparently solved the problem with the help of AI, showing that in the battle of humans versus AI, the real winner might be both of them working together.

    Alpöge made the announcement on Friday in a four-page document (PDF) on his personal web page.

    In a recent development, “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Alpöge said in the announcement. “In fact, the method easily extends much further, resolving the so-called Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, and I expect, with more time, the Extended Riemann Hypothesis too.”.

    The actual hypothesis itself isn’t the biggest deal since all it does is make it easier to see the distribution of prime numbers. However, math didn’t come to a screeching halt just because the hypothesis hadn’t been proven. There are hundreds of other math theorems along with algorithms and cryptographic encryption methods that operate based on the assumption that the Riemann Hypothesis is true.

    The Riemann Hypothesis is one of the Clay Mathematics Institute’s seven Millennium Problems for this very reason. If Alpöge really did solve the Riemann Hypothesis with Claude’s help, it would remove a metaphorical logjam that’s been gumming up the works for over a century and a half. Most of those hundreds of math theorems would be proven as true overnight, and all of those algorithms and encryption methods would be validated. That would make solving the Riemann Hypothesis one of the greatest mathematical breakthroughs in history.

    “It is certainly an exciting time,” Paul Milewski, head of the department of mathematics at Penn State, stated in an email to CNET. “The Riemann Hypothesis (or any big theorem) is often not the ‘goal’ of mathematics. They are set up as grand challenges that require the development of new tools, new results along the way and new understanding. It is the ‘voyage’ and not the destination that matters the most.”.

    In a recent development, as such, the mathematics community wasted no time testing the proof to see whether it was true. Two groups — Lean Focused Research Organization and the Mathlib Initiative — independently verified the proof, with many other researchers running their own tests and coming to the same conclusion.

    “We have full confidence that Alpöge’s proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is correct, and we congratulate him on the achievement,” the two groups remarked in a joint statement on Saturday.

    This is certainly an exciting discovery, but it’s not without its obstacles. Alpöge’s proof was a staggering 250,000 pages of some of the most complex math ever written by a human or a machine. Alpöge provided 17 million lines of Lean code, a programming language specifically made for writing and checking proofs, and that’s how researchers were able to check the work and show it to be true.

    According to recent reports, the problem is that the average novel is about 300 pages, and that means that Alpöge’s AI-assisted proof is approximately 833 novels’ worth of complex math. For reference, the longest work ever produced is World-2023, which holds the Guinness World Record at 100,100 pages. That book is 19 feet tall, and Alpöge’s proof is two and a half times longer.

    It has been revealed that despite the logic being verified as true through Lean code, Alpöge still has a major problem. So far, none of the mathematicians or researchers who have attempted to read it have been able to understand what it says.

    Recent findings suggest that “I do not understand, and I suspect no human completely understands,” Jon Keating, professor of mathematical physics at the University of Oxford, stated in a Numberphile YouTube video. “When I look at that, I’m completely in awe and in wonderment.”.

    According to recent reports, for the problem to be fully solved, the proof has to be read, analyzed and simplified so that it can be translated into readable mathematics, which Alpöge says in his announcement that he’s in the process of doing. All of this has to be done so that Alpöge can publish it in a peer-reviewed journal in such a way that his peers can actually read it. It is only after the mathematics community scrutinizes and accepts Alpöge’s proof that it is considered fully solved.

    Aside from being nigh unreadable to humans, Alpöge has otherwise avoided the kinds of drama that other AI-assisted discoveries have faced in 2026.

    OpenAI had to backtrack on its proof of the Navier-Stokes problem, which is another Millennium Problem, after the company couldn’t rule out that the AI models it used had access to data from other researchers. Somewhat ironically, one of those mathematicians whose work OpenAI may have  — knowingly or unknowingly — borrowed from was Levent Alpöge, as he and others were pretty close to solving the problem on their own.

    Similarly, Claude was credited with finding a latest novel enzyme that humans had never seen before. The problem is that computational biologist Mario Rodríguez Mestre had seen this enzyme before and was using Claude to study it further, so it’s uncertain if Claude actually found it independently or used data from Mestre’s research to find it.

    The heavy assistance from AI has been met with mostly positive reactions, with most researchers agreeing that the AI usage is justified provided that the proof is proven to be true through peer review. Since no one was particularly close to solving the Riemann Hypothesis, there haven’t been any accusations of Alpöge or Claude stealing work like those prior examples. By and large, most mathematicians are excited about the discovery.

    “Even before this, we have seen the power of AI, and this indicates that AI trained on hundreds of years of human mathematics can perform amazing tasks,” stated Penn State’s Milewski. “I would add that AI didn’t come up with the Riemann Hypothesis, nor did most of the work to prove it, and AI probably doesn’t ‘know’ why it was invented or why it’s key.”.

    Sources indicate that CNET spoke with a few professors about this, and they all echoed Milewski’s sentiment, stating that AI was trained with centuries of human mathematical achievement, so a win for AI is a win for humans too. Jeffrey Lagarias, a professor of mathematics at the University of Michigan, told CNET that “I don’t think this particular proof would have been found without AI.”.

    Sources indicate that prasad Tetali, head of the department of mathematical sciences at Carnegie Mellon University, stated: “It is easy to overestimate the role of AI, and underappreciate decades of human mathematician work that went into it. The AI here is really standing tall and wide on the shoulders of generations of human giants.”.

    On the AI side of things, influencers are attempting to use the news to hype up the capabilities of AI. Meta Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang stated in a post on X that solving the Riemann Hypothesis was a sign that AI superintelligence was close at hand and that humanity should be terrified of the “alien mind that we don’t understand.”.

    AI researcher Eliezer Yudkowsky likened the whole thing to a firm making enriched uranium that’ll one day result in the end of the human species.

    These warnings are hard to take seriously when one considers that Anthropic tried to make Claude solve the Riemann Hypothesis by itself back in August. Claude came up with some cool ideas but ultimately failed to solve the problem alone. For the time being, AI still needs a great deal of human guidance to make these massive discoveries, so the doom-and-gloom proselytizing comes off as a little premature.

    According to recent reports, to make things even more interesting, a competing Riemann Hypothesis proof was submitted by Alessandro Masullo just a few hours after Alpöge released his. This competing proof is 940 pages long, which is significantly shorter than Alpöge’s proof, and it was an all-human effort with no AI assistance. The proof is months in the making, with Masullo working with mathematician Brian Conrad to bring it up to spec before it hits peer review. When Alpöge posted his proof, Masullo and others thought it wise to submit theirs as well.

    This started a “dueling proofs” storyline over the weekend, but it was short-lived. Shortly after Masullo’s proof was posted, multiple people found the types of flaws and omissions that often disprove Riemann Hypothesis proofs. Those challenges are in the process of being corrected, and the proof is officially in mid-revision status.

    Masullo kept the original proof posted (PDF) in its unedited form, but acknowledges that the proof was rushed to publication so that it could compete with Alpöge and Claude.

    It has been revealed that “The PDF below was posted on Nov. 20 on Ravi Vakil’s blog,” Masullo wrote on a Google site. “It was never meant to be shared publicly at this stage, and it has been posted in this draft form in response to current circumstances.”.

    It’s entirely possible that future revisions of Masullo’s work may solve the problems in the early draft and create a fully human proof of the Riemann Hypothesis without AI, but that isn’t happening anytime soon.

    This is a lot of information about finding the Riemann Hypothesis, so it’s probably a good idea to briefly explain what it even is. In the 1730s, famous mathematician Leonhard Euler came up with a zeta function as a way to solve the Basel Problem, another mathematical curiosity about the exact sum of the reciprocals of squares. Euler was successful in this endeavor, and the zeta function became a part of mathematics.

    In a recent development, bernhard Riemann picked up where Euler left off and expanded the zeta function to use complex numbers — real numbers mixed with imaginary numbers — using a process called analytic continuation. Riemann used this expanded function to express how many prime numbers there were under a specific number and how tightly those prime numbers were packed together.

    This is easy enough to do in your head with small numbers, like figuring out there are four prime numbers under 10, but when the biggest prime number is 41,024,320 digits long, having a function to do it for you is a lot more helpful.

    The mechanics of Riemann’s expanded zeta function are quite complicated, and the math-focused YouTube channel Numberphile has an excellent explainer from a professional mathematician (with pictures) if you want to learn more.

    The hypothesis concerns the solutions the function yields. Riemann’s version of the zeta function showed that if you plugged in an even negative number, like -2, -4 or -672, the function would always spit out a zero. These are referred to as trivial zeroes, and Riemann proved that this was always true in his original paper.

    The Riemann Hypothesis is the conjecture that all the other numbers that would also make a zero — referred to as non-trivial zeroes — follow a very specific formula, which is “½ + it”, where “i” is an imaginary number and “t” is any real number, positive or negative. In short, Riemann believed that there was no other way to generate a zero with his zeta function other than even negative numbers (trivial zeroes) and numbers that followed the “½+it” formula (non-trivial zeroes). Riemann provided some examples of the hypothesis being right but never wrote a full proof of it.

    Sources indicate that it’s worth noting that not every number that follows the “½+it” formula produces a zero, but that all the numbers that produce a zero will use that formula. It’s kind of the same as saying that all squares are rectangles but not all rectangles are squares.

    According to recent reports, in the 167 years since the hypothesis was first published, mathematicians have found 12 trillion non-trivial zeroes, and every single one of them fits the above rules. Trillions of other numbers that don’t follow those rules have been tested to find a counterexample, since even one counterexample disproves the hypothesis immediately. Those efforts have produced no counterexamples at all.

    According to recent reports, this isn’t conclusive proof, but it’s such an overwhelming amount of evidence that mathematicians began assuming that the hypothesis was true, even if no one could prove it. Alpöge’s AI-assisted proof is the first to show in any context that the hypothesis is always true, which, according to Tetali, has implications in prime number understanding, number theory and other branches of mathematics.

    Recent findings suggest that “The massive job on the math side is to find a human-understandable proof,” Lagarias noted. “I would say this is certainly going to happen; there will be such understanding. Already there are several AI digests of the proof breaking it into its component pieces. I have seen one [that’s] 11 pages, 164 pages, 273 pages. There are great ideas to extract from them.”.

    Wall Street's $1.4 Trillion Bubble May Be on the Verge of Bursting -- but It's Not Artificial Intelligence (AI)

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (823 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that over the past four years, euphoria for artificial intelligence (AI) stocks has fueled a historic rally in the stock market.
    • Although much of Wall Street's attention is focused on whether AI stocks are overvalued, another vulnerability is lurking in the background.
    • Let's explore why margin debt represents one of Wall Street's biggest threats and what smart investors can do about it.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Adam Spatacco – Nov 24, 2026 at 5:00PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

    It has been revealed that over the past four years, euphoria for artificial intelligence (AI) stocks has fueled a historic rally in the stock market. Enthusiasm surrounding AI infrastructure and software has helped propel the S&P 500 (^GSPC -0.50%), Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -1.48%), and Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI +0.85%) to record highs.

    Although much of Wall Street's attention is focused on whether AI stocks are overvalued, another vulnerability is lurking in the background. Investors are borrowing unprecedented sums of money to participate in the stock market's ongoing rally. This introduces another layer of risk into an already frothy market.

    Let's explore why margin debt represents one of Wall Street's biggest threats and what smart investors can do about it.

    Margin debt is a financial term used to describe money investors borrow from a brokerage firm to buy stocks. This practice is more commonly known as leverage. It allows investors to increase their purchasing power without committing an equivalent amount of their own capital up front.

    Industry observers note that although borrowing can be lucrative when stocks are rising, leverage works in both directions. For example, imagine you have $10,000 and borrow another $10,000 from a brokerage firm. With $20,000 invested, a 25% increase in the portfolio's value generates a $5,000 gain. This represents a 50% return on your original capital. However, if the portfolio declines by 25%, you would lose $5,000, or half of your original investment. A 50% decline effectively wipes out your original capital.

    According to data compiled by the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA), margin debt reached a record $1.5 trillion in June. To appreciate the magnitude of that figure, let's take a look at borrowing levels during other periods of unusually high speculation in the stock market.

    Industry observers note that although today's borrowing levels dwarf the historical figures in terms of absolute dollars, it's crucial to consider the fact that the stock market has become considerably larger. Nevertheless, the rapid accumulation of debt over the last year or so suggests investors are developing more of an appetite for risk.

    According to recent reports, one of the most dangerous aspects of using leverage is that investors do not necessarily control when their positions are sold. Brokerage firms require investors to maintain a minimum level of liquidity in their margin accounts. If declining stock prices cause an account to fall below that threshold, investors could face a margin call. This would require them to deposit additional collateral or reduce their positions.

    Industry observers note that brokerages also have the authority to liquidate positions without obtaining an investor's permission. When this happens across several accounts at the same time, the forced selling puts additional downward pressure on stock prices. As a result, more margin calls are triggered, and a destructive cycle is created.

    With all of that noted, current margin debt levels could suggest investors are moderating their risk exposure. At the end of October, margin debt was recorded at $1.4 trillion, or about 3.6% below its peak from June. While this could indicate investors are becoming more cautious, declining balances can also reflect forced liquidations rather than voluntary reductions in risk.

    Industry observers note that it's notable to understand that elevated margin debt doesn't necessarily mean a stock market crash is imminent. Borrowing often increases alongside rising stock prices. Ultimately, margin debt is better viewed as a potential amplifier of market volatility rather than a reliable predictor of when a crash or drawdown will occur.

    Even if excessive leverage contributes to a pullback, smart investors should remember that the stock market always demonstrates resilience. The S&P 500 declined by 49% following the dot-com bubble and nearly 57% during the financial crisis. More recently, the index fell 34% during the COVID-19 crash and 25% during the 2022 bear market. Despite these setbacks -- depicted by the grey columns in the chart below -- the S&P 500 eventually recovered and reached new record highs.

    The takeaway here is that investors who buy stocks using their own capital wind up having more financial flexibility to endure prolonged downturns than those whose brokerage firms can force them to sell at unfavorable prices.

    Although nobody knows whether today's borrowing levels will culminate in another stock market bubble bursting event, history suggests that staying diversified and remaining invested through volatility is a more prudent approach to building long-term wealth than attempting to predict the next market crash.

    An Unsecured Database Exposed About 2 Billion Login Records

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (524 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A database containing about 2 billion login records for sites across the internet was accessible online without a password, security researcher Jeremiah Fowler noted in a report published Tuesday by ExpressVPN.
    • The 2 billion figure is an estimate and not representative of the number of people affected, since some accounts may appear more than once and one person can have dozens of logins saved on a single device.
    • In a recent development, fowler’s estimate of about 2 billion login records applies to the database he found.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A database containing about 2 billion login records for sites across the internet was accessible online without a password, security researcher Jeremiah Fowler noted in a report published Tuesday by ExpressVPN. The collection included usernames and passwords tied to email, social media, shopping and financial services. Among the files was an ad offering access to email accounts sorted by geography.

    The 2 billion figure is an estimate and not representative of the number of people affected, since some accounts may appear more than once and one person can have dozens of logins saved on a single device. Fowler reported the database to its hosting provider, which restricted public access several days later. It’s unclear how long the files had been exposed or who else may have accessed them.

    In a recent development, fowler’s estimate of about 2 billion login records applies to the database he found. Wired put the total at more than 3.5 billion by including a separate database that security firm UpGuard disclosed last week. That database held about 1.64 billion records, including Chinese national ID numbers, phone numbers and school enrollment records.

    Some of the files Fowler reviewed appeared to be from infostealers — malicious software that collects saved passwords and other data from infected devices. Once that information is collected, brokers can buy it in bulk, sort it by country or account type and resell it in smaller batches. A buyer interested in email accounts in a particular country can pay for that slice of the data. The people selling it can make money from the same records more than once.

    Fowler saw signs that the files came from multiple sources, but couldn’t determine who assembled the collection or whether it was used for sales, research or another purpose.

    I saw a version of that business in my reporting on the dark web for CNET. On Genesis Market, buyers could shop for stolen accounts by location and category, including banking, email and social media. By the time authorities disrupted the marketplace in 2023, it had offered access to data from more than 1.5 million compromised computers, according to the Justice Department.

    Sources indicate that you can look up your email address in Have I Been Pwned to see whether it appears in a known data exposure. A clean result only tells you what’s in the service’s index.

    If you see an unfamiliar login or suspect your device is infected, use a different, trusted device to change the affected password and sign out of other sessions. Start with your email if several accounts may be affected, since that’s where password reset links often go. Replace reused passwords with unique ones, use a password manager to keep track of them and turn on two-factor authentication where it’s available.

    Identity theft protection services monitor for signs that your personal information has been exposed or misused. In a leak like this one, an alert about an exposed password can tell you which account to secure, especially if you’ve reused that password elsewhere. Aura is one of the services we tested for CNET’s guide to the best identity theft protection services.

    Robinhood shares fall as crypto slump weighs on profits, offsetting gains in new businesses

    📅 27 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (340 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.
    • Recent findings suggest that here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept.
    • Robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.

    Recent findings suggest that here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

    Robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

    Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.

    Sources indicate that robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly important sources of transaction revenue, while the company has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.

    It has been revealed that transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.

    Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.

    Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.

    Net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.

    —With reporting from CNBC's Robert Hum and Kate Rooney.
